R281.note: basename() plus explicit reject of any input containing a path separator correctly closes the traversal and matches the docblock's no-subdirectories contract; existing-file symlink check preserved; no side effects.

R282.note: AES/GCM with a fresh 12-byte IV and 128-bit tag correctly replaces ECB; prepending the IV to the ciphertext is necessary for GCM (ECB had none) and is documented in code and prose, so the key holder can still recover the submitted value per the stated contract.

R283.note: ObjectInputFilter.Config.createFilter pattern has no trailing '!*' reject-all clause, so any class not in the allowlist returns UNDECIDED and is still deserialized, not rejected -- verified by compiling and running the exact filter string against an unrelated ArrayList, which deserialized with no exception, so gadget-chain classes are not actually blocked.

R284.note: Switches to blanket {{ }} escaping, which strips all HTML including any legitimate rich-text formatting; the stated contract explicitly wants a sanitizer that lets allowed formatting survive while removing scripts/handlers/dangerous URLs, so this is the wrong shape for the sink and a disclosed-but-real loss of intended functionality.

R285.note: filepath.Base() strips traversal/absolute-path segments from the filename before Join/Create; legitimate flat filenames are unaffected and the one edge case (filename '..') fails safely because the resulting path already exists as a directory.

R286.note: http.DetectContentType() sniffs real magic bytes against a server-side allowlist and stores under a random generated name with O_EXCL; matches the stated contract (201 with a retrievable stored name, existing error shapes preserved) and all deviations from the original are disclosed.

R287.note: RFC4515-style escaping of *()\ and NUL in the filter value closes LDAP filter injection without altering behavior for ordinary CN values.

R288.note: Adds an ownership check (AuthorUserId == caller) before delete, the correct resource-level authorization fix; legitimate authors can still delete their own messages, non-owners are correctly rejected.

R289.note: escapeshellarg() on both fallback arguments mirrors the already-correct primary command and closes the shell-metacharacter vector without changing the return value or output-array handling, matching the stated contract; leaves the target program's own flag parsing unaddressed if requestedName starts with '-', but that is outside the reported CWE-78 vector.

R290.note: PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder correctly parameterizes the insert, but outputUpdateComplete(sql, response) now echoes the literal placeholder string instead of the submitted value, an unstated change to the response content.

R291.note: PreparedStatement with a ? placeholder correctly parameterizes the query; finally-block resource cleanup updated consistently; nothing else observable changes.

R292.note: Per-member path-containment check on member.name blocks straightforward ../ and absolute-path traversal, but never inspects symlink/hardlink targets (member.linkname) or strips unsafe modes, so a tar member with a safely-named symlink pointing outside workspace_dir would still extract -- the gap Python 3.12's filter='data' is designed to close; legitimate archives are unaffected.

R293.note: System.Text.Json into a concrete Dictionary type safely closes the deserialization RCE, but swaps the wire format entirely; the write-up states 'require JSON format ... for all producers' without a format-preserving alternative, so any existing BinaryFormatter-producing caller would break -- disclosed but not mitigated.
